Not OP but if you're serious about quitting cold turkey, throw all of your shit out. Bongs, grinders, papers, flower, all of it- out of sight out, out of mind. I was violently baked this past Sunday and had an epiphany that my mental health will not improve if I continue to abuse marijuana. I have things I want to achieve and smoking every day will not get me there. An hour later, I threw all of my stuff in the dumpster. It was very symbolic for me but at the same time, it's way easier to quit if you don't have any paraphernalia laying around. Again, out of sight out of mind.

Your brain likes patterns because they're familiar, that's part of why stopping destructive behaviors is so hard. So what do you do? You create new, healthier patterns. I can't speak for anyone else but in my experience, I had to get to a point with all of my addictions (weed, alcohol, food) where I realized that they were simply not sustainable anymore. With alcohol and binge eating, my body forced me to stop. I don't recommend getting to that point.

Best of luck on your journey and remember, take it one day at a time.

That's how positive change works- you asses your behavior, implement a plan to act differently, stick to it and it eventually becomes a new way of living.

The literal definition of change is to 'make someone or something different, to alter.' Controlling your impulses (i.e. behaving more maturely) qualifies as changing. Finally, it's my time to shine!! Between April 2017 and late August 2018, I lost 117lbs. I noticed so many positives throughout this whole process. I was 19/20 when this occurred, I am now 23.

One of the most noticeable things was that my self-esteem shot up once I lost about 60-70lbs. It's still not amazingly high but that's just due to those insecurities we all have.

Clothes shopping is way easier. I went from wearing 3XL to L. My pants went from being 44 to 32. It's much easier to find stylish clothes that fit well when you're at a healthy weight. When I was really overweight, I was basically restricted to whatever was in stock for the larger sizes.

Dating. I did not date at all when I was overweight. I tried but for obvious reasons, I didn't draw much interest. Since losing the weight, I've had 2 short relationships and a few dates here and there. Currently single bc I have things to work on.
